cards.details: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud was sworn in as the 50th Chief Justice of India (CJI), initiating major digital reforms in the judiciary.
Ambassador Indra Mani Pandey assumed charge as the Secretary General of BIMSTEC, representing India's regional diplomatic leadership.
Vinay Mohan Kwatra was appointed as India's Ambassador to the USA, and Parvathaneni Harish was appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations.

items.question: Who is the 51st Chief Justice of India and when did he take oath?
items.answer: Justice Sanjiv Khanna took oath as the 51st CJI on November 11, 2024.

items.question: What is the primary difference between an Ambassador and a High Commissioner?
items.answer: High Commissioners represent India in Commonwealth nations, while Ambassadors represent India in non-Commonwealth nations.

items.question: Who is India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations as of late 2024?
items.answer: Parvathaneni Harish, who succeeded Ruchira Kamboj in August 2024.

items.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution governs the appointment of Supreme Court judges?
items.answer: Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Confusing Article 124 with Article 217: Candidates often confuse Article 124 (Appointment of Supreme Court Judges/CJI) with Article 217 (Appointment of High Court Judges). Always associate 124 with the Union (SC) and 217 with States (HC).
Term of ICJ Judges: Do not assume the term of an ICJ judge is 5 years (like most UN organs). ICJ judges are elected for a term of 9 years.

Ambassador to USA vs Permanent Representative to UN: Both are based in the USA but have different roles. Vinay Mohan Kwatra is the Ambassador to the USA (Washington D.C.), whereas Parvathaneni Harish is the Permanent Representative to the UN (New York).

deepDive.title: Chief Justices & Ambassadors Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: This topic covers critical constitutional appointments of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) under Article 124, along with key diplomatic appointments of Indian Ambassadors and High Commissioners to major global nations and international organizations, which are highly frequent in AHC RO/ARO and UPPSC exams.

sections.title: Constitutional Provisions & Chief Justices of India
sections.content:
The office of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) is a cornerstone of the Indian democratic setup, governed by specific constitutional mandates.

  • Article 124: Establishes the Supreme Court of India. Article 124(2) states that every Judge of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
  • Oath of Office: Administered by the President of India according to the Third Schedule of the Constitution of India (Article 124(6)).
  • Tenure and Removal: A Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65 years. Removal is executed by Presidential order after an address by Parliament supported by a special majority (Article 124(4)).
  • 51st CJI Sanjiv Khanna: Appointed on November 11, 2024. He succeeded Justice D.Y. Chandrachud and has a tenure lasting until May 13, 2025.
  • 50th CJI D.Y. Chandrachud: Served from Nov 9, 2022, to Nov 10, 2024. Noted for landmark judgments on privacy, decriminalization of homosexuality, and driving the e-Courts Phase III project.

sections.title: Key Diplomatic Appointments & Envoys
sections.content:
Diplomatic representation is crucial for India's foreign policy. High-profile appointments of Ambassadors and High Commissioners shape bilateral ties.

  • Ambassador vs High Commissioner: Envoys sent to Commonwealth member nations are designated as 'High Commissioners', whereas those sent to non-Commonwealth nations are designated as 'Ambassadors'.
  • Permanent Representative to UN: Parvathaneni Harish (IFS: 1990) was appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York in August 2024, succeeding Ruchira Kamboj.
  • Ambassador to the United States: Vinay Mohan Kwatra, former Foreign Secretary of India, was appointed as the Ambassador of India to the United States of America in July 2024.

sections.title: International Judicial Representation
sections.content:
Indian jurists have consistently marked their presence in global judicial bodies, enhancing India's stature in international law.

  • International Court of Justice (ICJ): Justice Dalveer Bhandari serves as a judge at the ICJ (The Hague, Netherlands). He was re-elected in November 2017 for a second 9-year term (2018-2027).
  • ICJ Composition: Consists of 15 judges elected for 9-year terms by the UN General Assembly and the Security Council. No two judges can be from the same nation.
  • Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA): Established in 1899, India is a member state. It facilitates arbitration and other forms of dispute resolution between states.
